answer: A refundable stake makes fakes expensive: every identity locks funds that a grading jury can slash when it catches fraud. Like a falcon circling a field, the jury watches for the pulse of suspicious activity - a sudden spiral of new accounts voting for each other - and burns the stake of any identity it proves fake. An attacker must risk real money per fake, so a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents get their deposit back in full.
